title: Qualify a prepared proposal before it says Ready
baseline_ref: brief/foundations (D-01 and F-01); Q-13 merges after F-01

status.capability_ready: validator and dry runner only; preparedOpportunities stays unsupported until F-09 registers a provider that uses them

ownership.independent_reviewer: pending; Lapo coordinates technical review and shared-file integration

behavior: qualifyPreparedProposal(request, services) returns ready, blocked or review_needed with coded one-line reasons and the exact snapshot judged: proposal revision, flow, version, version digest, bindings and a fingerprint.

Source access and required account/target: every connection and machine the graph binds must be available, shown on the proposal and unchanged; connection lookups are project-scoped and metadata only.

Exact version: the live digest(version.trigger), the identity the effect boundary records, must equal the pinned one; versionReadiness must pass; the composition record must be VALIDATED and named by the flow; the goal must be active at the prepared revision.
Deliveries need a real recipient: an empty list (which readiness accepts), a missing prop or a placeholder blocks.

Authority behavior is predicted with the effect boundary's own fold for the workflow principal; a refusal blocks; CODE, ungoverned pieces, agents, nested workflows and runtime-gated tools need review.
Typed job constraints: review_before_effects (used by every opportunity kind), forbid, recipients and unverified.

Previews: the basis must be backed by evidence; every effect is described once; 'asks first' must match Authority; 'simulated' needs the dry sample to reach the step; 'completed' needs a succeeded effect record from a run proven to be this version.
recheckQualification returns stale when the fingerprint changes; briefReadiness maps only a current ready qualification to F-01 ready.

PreparedDryRunner runs the exact version once in the real engine on a fixture with every reachable service simulated, on a scratch copy deleted afterwards, never through the job queue; a graph it supports needs a successful sample before Ready.

Both modules join the #573 workflow data-plane inventory (src/workflows/adapters/untrusted-reach.test.ts): the qualification module reads only graph, ids, state and effect digests; the dry runner returns its own simulated run's bounded step outputs to a person-facing preview, which a model consumer must frame.

migration: None. No schema, data, route or daemon wiring change; nothing calls the validator until F-09.
rollback: Revert the Q-13 commit. No other code references the new modules.
limitations: Only typed constraints are checked; free-text conditions need an unverified constraint.
Placeholder recipients are a fixed list; recipients computed at run time are checked at dispatch.
A connection's revision excludes its updated time so token refreshes do not invalidate proposals; re-authorizing a different account under the same row is not detected.
A dry run shows the version executes on its fixture, not that a real model's draft is good; Q-01 and Q-02 measure that.
found: Readiness treats an empty required collection as present, so a Gmail send with receiver [] passes readiness. That is deliberate for collections in general; Q-13 blocks it for deliveries and leaves readiness unchanged.
